chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Khuzai, from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Saie, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

My father wrote in his letter to me, and I asked him about the testimony for them: So establish the testimony for the sake of Allah, even if it be against yourself, or the parents, and the near-relatives, regarding what is between you and them. But if you fear injustice for your brother (in faith), then no (do not testify).

key_terms.أَخ: brother in faith, a fellow Muslim believer
key_terms.شَهَادَة: testimony or legal witnessing; a formal statement given before a judge in Islamic law
key_terms.ضَيْم: injustice, oppression, or wrongful harm suffered

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Kadhim say about the obligation to give testimony in Islamic law even against one's own family?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a letter from an Imam to his son conveying a nuanced ruling on testimony (shahadah) in legal disputes. The primary command mirrors Quran 4:135, calling believers to uphold testimony for Allah's sake even against oneself or one's closest kin. However, the hadith adds a crucial exception from the Shia jurisprudential tradition: if a believer fears that giving testimony would result in injustice being inflicted on a fellow Muslim, then withholding testimony becomes permissible or even required. This balance between impartial justice and protection of the community reflects the Imams' sophisticated approach to jurisprudential ethics.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ismail Biin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Mansour Al Khazaie, from Ali Bin Suweyd Al Saie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said:

‘My father wrote in his letter to me<sup>asws</sup>, and I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the testimony for them: ‘So establish the testimony for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> even though it be against yourself, or the parents, and the near-relatives, with regards to what is between you and them. So if you fear injustice against your brother, so no (don’t come forward)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Khuza‘iy from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Sa’iy who has narrated the following: “My father wrote to me in his letter and I asked abu al-Hassan, Alayhi al-Salam, about testimony for them. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must present a testimony for Allah, even if it is against your own soul or parents or relatives between you and them, but if you fear injustice to your brother then do not do so.’”
Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdiy from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran a similar Hadith.
